page: Amazon Web Services x2iedn.24xlarge is an extreme memory-optimized instance engineered for memory-intensive workloads and in-memory analytics. Operating on the AWS Nitro system, it features 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores powered by 3.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8375C processors based on the x86_64 architecture. Memory density is exceptionally high, supplying 3072 GB of DDR4 RAM clocked at 3 GHz, which equates to 32 GB per vCPU. The instance also includes 2850 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and provides a 75 Gbps baseline network interface.

In benchmark evaluations, the x2iedn.24xlarge shows strong parallel computing and memory throughput capabilities. PassMark CPU encryption tests reached top-tier standing at 86,373.49, complemented by strong multi-core results including a PassMark CPU score of 74,908.92 and a stress-ng multi-core figure of 92,868.95. Memory bandwidth reaches 296.57 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 5,008.9 GB/sec for small cached reads. These throughput capabilities translate into strong database execution, with PassMark database operations scoring 29,638.46 and Redis handling 88.2 million SET operations per second. Conversely, single-thread performance registers in the middle tier, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1589.0 and a stress-ng single-core result of 1891.98.

The instance provides high resource consolidation efficiency for enterprise workloads that require massive amounts of RAM relative to CPU counts. While per-instance deployment represents a substantial commitment, the 32:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio mitigates the need to over-provision computing cores merely to satisfy memory requirements. With 2850 GB of integrated NVMe SSD storage and 75 Gbps network connectivity, the system is well aligned for large-scale in-memory databases like Redis and SAP HANA, distributed caching tiers, real-time analytics, and heavy relational database management systems.
